title: Devissage for coherent properties with a prescribed support subset
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $S\subseteq |X|$ be any subset, not necessarily closed. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $\operatorname{Supp}(F)=\{x\in X:F_x\ne0\}$, where $F_x$ is its module stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] supported in $S$. Assume that $\mathcal P(0)$, that $\mathcal P$ is invariant under isomorphisms between these modules, and that for every short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3\to0$ of coherent modules supported in $S$, $\mathcal P(F_1)$ and $\mathcal P(F_3)$ imply $\mathcal P(F_2)$. Assume also that for every closed immersion $j:W\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] from an integral scheme $W$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] with $j(W)\subseteq S$, and every nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $J\subseteq\mathcal O_W$, $\mathcal P(j_*J)$ holds; $j_*$ denotes module pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $\mathcal P(F)$ holds for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ supported in $S$.

proof.text: Fix a coherent $F$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(F)\subseteq S$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] to the Noetherian scheme $X$ and $F$. Obtain $0=F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_m=F$ with coherent $F_j$ and $Q_j=F_j/F_{j-1}\cong(i_j)_*I_j$, where $i_j:Z_j\to X$ is a closed immersion, $Z_j$ is integral and $I_j$ is a nonzero coherent ideal. Each $Q_j$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum](1). Thus $0\to F_{j-1}\to F_j\to Q_j\to0$ is a short exact sequence of coherent modules. Length $m=0$ is allowed.

proof.text: For every $x\notin S$, $F_x=0$. The injection $(F_j)_x\hookrightarrow F_x$ and the formula $(Q_j)_x\cong(F_j)_x/(F_{j-1})_x$ from [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](1),(3) give $(F_j)_x=(Q_j)_x=0$. Consequently every $F_j$ and $Q_j$ is supported in $S$. The isomorphism $Q_j\cong(i_j)_*I_j$ also induces stalk isomorphisms, so $(i_j)_*I_j$ is supported in $S$.

proof.text: Fix a factor and write $i:Z\to X$, $I=I_j$, $Q=Q_j$. A closed immersion is locally of finite type: on affine charts it is induced by a quotient algebra, generated over its source ring by the empty family [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes $Z$ locally Noetherian. Thus $I$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. If $\eta$ is the generic point of $Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk] gives $I_\eta\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2) and $Q\cong i_*I$, this puts $i(\eta)$ in $\operatorname{Supp}(Q)$. Coherence of $Q$ and [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] make $Q$ quasi-coherent of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed] makes its support closed. A closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its closed image; hence $\overline{\{i(\eta)\}}=i(Z)$, because $\overline{\{\eta\}}=Z$. The closed support of $Q$ therefore contains $i(Z)$. Conversely the pushforward stalks vanish outside $i(Z)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](1), so $\operatorname{Supp}(Q)=i(Z)\subseteq S$. The hypothesis on nonzero quasi-coherent ideals now gives $\mathcal P(i_*I)$, and isomorphism invariance gives $\mathcal P(Q)$.

proof.text: Induct on $j=0,\ldots,m$. The base $\mathcal P(F_0)=\mathcal P(0)$ is assumed. At stage $j\ge1$ the preceding steps give $\mathcal P(Q_j)$ and ensure that the coherent terms of $0\to F_{j-1}\to F_j\to Q_j\to0$ are supported in $S$. The induction hypothesis and the extension assumption give $\mathcal P(F_j)$. For $j=m$ this is $\mathcal P(F)$. This also handles $F=0$, $S=\varnothing$, and $X=\varnothing$ without assuming the existence of any integral subscheme.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q38-9e4a69923 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full: a 4-step filtration proof with no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint.from are unchanged from the unsplit base, and it is not a 2026-10-21 re-split. Source check: coherent.tex lemma-property-initial 01YG (l.3144) and lemma-property-irreducible 01YH. The item is the 01YG argument with supports in an arbitrary subset S; the zero ideal is replaced by P(0) and isomorphism invariance is assumed. This serves both uses in Q63's parent lem-pc-coherent-property-irreducible (S=T minus xi, and S=T). Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes gives a coherent chain with quotients isomorphic to (i_j)_*I_j, I_j nonzero and coherent; kernel-cokernel-sum(1) makes the quotients coherent. Step 2: module-stalk-exact (1) and (3) give vanishing of the submodule and quotient stalks outside S; elementary. Step 3: a closed immersion is locally of finite type (from def-weil-closed-immersion), so 01T6 makes Z locally Noetherian; 01XZ makes I quasi-coherent; ideal-generic-stalk (a)=>(c) gives I_eta nonzero; closed-pushforward-stalks (2) puts i(eta) in Supp(Q); 056J makes Supp(Q) closed; the homeomorphism onto the closed image gives the closure of i(eta) equal to i(Z); part (1) of the pushforward node gives Supp(Q)=i(Z) inside S; then the hypothesis applies, and isomorphism invariance gives P(Q). Every cited statement says what is used, and closedness of S is never used. Step 4 is an explicit induction with base P(0). Small cases: empty X, empty S or F=0; Spec k[eps]; the affine line with S the generic point, where only F=0 is supported in S; zero-dimensional factors. The statement is true. Duplicates: the 01YL-type, two-of-three and algebraic-space devissage nodes and the e2/s3 filtrations differ, so same_as=[] is right. I accept the 8 declared tool_uses: generic module and scheme tools from sk-thm-p1 and pqf; the same-unit e2 filtration lacks the nonzero and coherence clauses, and the unit's 02O5 route is not replaced. lean.statement: theorem coherent_supported_property_devissage (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (S : Set X) (P : X.Modules → Prop) (hP_zero : P (0 : X.Modules)) (hP_iso : ∀ (F G : X.Modules) (_e : F ≅ G), RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace G → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ S → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (G.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ S → P F → P G) (hP_extension : ∀ T : ShortComplex X.Modules, T.ShortExact → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace T.X₁ → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace T.X₂ → RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace T.X₃ → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (T.X₁.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ S → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (T.X₂.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ S → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (T.X₃.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ S → P T.X₁ → P T.X₃ → P T.X₂) (hP_integral : ∀ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion j → IsIntegral W → Set.range j.base ⊆ S → ∀ J : W.IdealSheafData, J ≠ ⊥ → P ((pushforward j).obj J.toModules)) : ∀ F : X.Modules, RingedSpace.IsCoherent X.toRingedSpace F → {x : X | ¬ Subsingleton (F.presheaf.stalk x)} ⊆ S → P F
